LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: RECIPE

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you write clear instructions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify components of a recipe for information
2. write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning
3. enjoy exploring various ways of preparing foods for cultural appreciation

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: RECIPE
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: RECIPE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify components of a recipe for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify components of a recipe for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify components of a recipe for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify components of a recipe for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Enjoy exploring various ways of preparing foods for cultural appreciation

What this means
In this part you learn to enjoy exploring various ways of preparing foods for cultural appreciation. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: enjoy exploring various ways of preparing foods for cultural appreciation.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can enjoy exploring various ways of preparing foods for cultural appreciation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify components of a recipe for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe to a partner. (skill: write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: enjoy exploring various ways of preparing foods for cultural appreciation)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify components of a recipe for information.
3. Practise this skill: write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning.
4. Practise this skill: enjoy exploring various ways of preparing foods for cultural appreciation.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you write clear instructions?
2. what went well and why?
3. what did not go well and why?
4. what can be done differently next time?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Recipe means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify components of a recipe for information.
5. Be able to: write a recipe of a cultural food for lifelong learning.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
